title: The heading at Cnoc fhiadhaich driven without props
summary: Under Henry Maddox's order to double the yield, the new gallery at Cnoc fhiadhaich is driven north along the seam on the pay of the ton, and the oak props from Cathair fhada stop at the head of the carters' drift. The agent of A' Chompanaidh writes that the heading will be timbered when the yield allows.

title: Raghnall asks three times for timber at the heading
summary: Between an Gearran and an Giblean the crew-leaders Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill and Ailean mac Dhùghaill ask the agent at Cnoc fhiadhaich three times for props over the heading, where the shale roof has turned the colour the hewers read as bad ground. The agent writes the asking in his book and answers that oak will come in the summer.

title: Old Dòmhnall says the words at the pit-mouth
summary: When the eleven are brought out of the fallen heading at Cnoc fhiadhaich, Dòmhnall, an old hewer of the custodians' cutting and father of Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill, says the words of the face at the mouth of the drift, and the old hewers take them up. They had not been said at that pit-mouth since it was opened.

title: The eleven buried at Muileann chrom
summary: The eleven dead of the fall at Cnoc fhiadhaich are buried in the ground above the mill at Muileann chrom on the fourth day after the fall. Marsaili nic Sheumais, keeper of the old cutting for Taigh na Fèithe, reads their names at the graves and writes each into the roll with father, mother and hearth, and the place as under the wild hill.

title: The fallen heading cleared and timbered
summary: The fall at Cnoc fhiadhaich is cleared by midsummer and the heading timbered pair by pair as it is cleared, with oak brought up from Cathair fhada in an t-Ògmhios. The crews are paid nothing for the days of digging, and the yield of the year is short.

title: Dòmhnall mac Raghnaill at the pit-mouth
summary: Dòmhnall, the six-year-old son of the crew-leader Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill, who had gone to the breakers' benches at Muileann chrom in the autumn, takes An Casad Tioram in am Màrt. He coughs nine nights on his father's knee and wakes well on the tenth morning, and goes back to the benches in the autumn.

title: The custodians ask that the breakers' benches be shut
summary: With the dry cough running through the summer among the children who break coal, the custodians of Taigh na Fèithe ask the agent of A' Chompanaidh to shut the benches at Muileann chrom and Cnoc fhiadhaich until it has passed. He writes the asking in his book, and the benches stay open to feed the pump furnaces.

title: The orphans carried to Cill thais
summary: In an t-Iuchar Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill drives fourteen orphans of the fall and the dry cough in a borrowed cart from Muileann chrom to Cill thais, two days west, with the crate of primers sent by A' Chompanaidh. The warden of Cill thais lifts each child down, has their names written, and sets the crate on a shelf of Taigh nan Dìlleachdan.

title: Hill coal burned for the lime of Baile ìseal
summary: The lime for the mortar of the tower at Baile ìseal is burned in a kiln on the shore with coal carted over the hills from Muileann chrom. The tower is built by the masons of the eastern coast of the grey stone of the cape, with a lamp sent by A' Chompanaidh.

title: The fishing families of Baile ìseal draw lots for the watches
summary: At the custodians' asking, the keeping of Taigh-solais Baile ìseal is given to the fishing households that had kept the driftwood fire on the cape. They draw lots for the watches at Samhain as they had drawn them for the fire, and the old fire is still lit beside the tower.

title: Torcall Clachair's last cairn
summary: Going home west from Baile ìseal in the spring after the lighting, Torcall Clachair has his cart stopped where the road tops the first rise of the moor and the tower first shows over the heather. Seated by the road, he lays a small cairn with his own hands from stones a boy brings from the ditch. He builds no more.

title: The hill crews go home to the harvest
summary: At the harvests after the fall and after the dry cough the crews of Muileann chrom and Cnoc fhiadhaich go home to their oats, a third of them the first year and half the second, and many stay home through the autumn. The yield of A' Chompanaidh in the hills falls short three years together.

title: Raghnall takes the leader's share
summary: The agent at Cnoc fhiadhaich offers Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill a leader's share on every ton his three crews raise, paid to him alone, if he keeps them at the face through harvest and winter; otherwise men of the coast will be brought up. Raghnall puts his mark to the paper in an Cèitean and keeps his crews below through the harvest.

title: Men of the foreshores shipped to Ceann òg
summary: In the autumn A' Chompanaidh gathers fishers and net-menders whose foreshores it has bought, ships them from the capital's quays in the traders' boats of Seòlaid Ceann òg round the western capes and up the Abhainn ìseal to Ceann òg, and walks them over the hills to the workings in companies of twenty with their families.

title: The first crews in the huts at Àth ìseal
summary: The first companies from the coast move into the plank huts at Àth ìseal, three long huts with a stove in each, a store and a well, with more rows pegged out beyond. The roll of Taigh na Fèithe notes that the camp has no custodian and has asked for none.
